I need the front end for Sorrel Practice. Practice software for solo registered dietitians that includes an AI assistant they can hand meal-planning and client-education tasks to, then check its work against the client's record before anything goes to the client.

Who's using it: Rebecca Haddad, RD, who runs a one-person telehealth nutrition practice specializing in digestive conditions. She sees about 22 clients a week and does her planning in the evenings.

What they're doing right now: Her new client Tom Brennan, 52, was diagnosed with IBS and starts the elimination phase of a low-FODMAP diet next Monday. Rebecca asked the assistant to draft a 14-day meal plan that fits his intake record, cooking skill and budget, with a shopping list and a one-page explainer. The assistant is about two-thirds through. It has drafted days 1–9 and paused to ask whether Tom's 'occasional lactose-free yogurt' means he tolerates it. Rebecca needs to answer, steer the remaining days, check which sources and rules each choice came from, catch anything that breaks his restrictions and accept or reject days individually before sending it Friday.

What's in the system at this point: Client record for Tom Brennan: IBS-D diagnosed Oct 2026, tree-nut allergy (cashew, pistachio), takes metformin 500 mg twice daily (prediabetes), works rotating shifts, cooks at a basic level, grocery budget about 120 a week, dislikes fish. Targets set by Rebecca: about 2,100 kcal, 95 g protein, fiber 25–30 g, carbohydrates spread evenly for blood-sugar control. Assistant task status: 9 of 14 days drafted with 3 meals and 2 snacks each, so 45 meal items in all. 3 items are flagged by the assistant itself: day 4 granola contains honey (high FODMAP), day 6 pesto may contain cashew, day 8 fiber at 19 g, below target. Each item cites its source, either the practice's own recipe bank (212 recipes) or a FODMAP serving-size reference, with the serving size used. Shopping list drafted for week 1 only, estimated at 104. Rebecca's earlier instruction: 'no recipes over 30 minutes on weekdays'.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
